A Black Hills Field Log

The Black HillsSouth Dakota

Dates  Sun Sep 13 – Fri Sep 18, 2026 Base camp  Black Forest Inn B&B · 23191 US-385 Drive  Twin Cities ↔ hills · ~9 hrs each way on I-90

Five days, one inn, and the whole range within an hour’s drive — radiating out in a new direction each day.

Book now

Wind Cave “Garden of Eden” tour — recreation.gov. Late-morning Mon. Sells out.

Passes

Custer SP $25/veh (7 days) · Badlands $30/veh · caves ticketed separately

Pack

Layers — days 60–70°F, nights 30–40s · caves 54°F · closed-toe shoes

On the road

Sunset ≈ 7:15 · keep 25+ yds from bison · they’re faster than they look

00
SUN · Sep 13

Arrive & settle in

  • From the CitiesI-90 west · ~9 hrs · arrive evening
  • TonightCheck in, meet Todd & Shelly
  • If daylight holdsRushmore ≈ 35 min south · open to 11 pm
  • DinnerHill City, ≈ 25 min

Getting in. You’ll come in from the east on I-90, and the Badlands and Wall Drug slide past your window in the last stretch — but save them for later in the week. Today is about reaching the inn after the roughly nine-hour haul from the Twin Cities.

Evening. Unpack, meet Todd & Shelly, breathe. If you somehow still have gas in the tank and daylight, Mount Rushmore is 35 minutes south and open until 11 pm. More likely: dinner in Hill City (Bumpin’ Buffalo or the Chute Rooster) and an early night.

01
MON · Sep 14

Caves & the granite core

  • Drive to cave≈ 1 h 15 south on US-385
  • BOOK AHEADWind Cave “Garden of Eden” tour · recreation.gov · ~$14/adult
  • Underground54°F · closed-toe shoes · no bags inside
  • Park passCuster State Park $25/vehicle — good all week

Morning. After breakfast, drive south to Wind Cave for a late-morning Garden of Eden Tour — the gentle one: about an hour, 150 steps spread along a short quarter-mile, riding the elevator down and back up rather than climbing. You still see the famous boxwork. Be on-site 30 minutes early; no refunds for late arrivals.

Afternoon. Wind Cave sits right below Custer State Park, so drift north into the adjacent Wildlife Loop — bison herds, pronghorn, prairie-dog towns, and the roadside “begging burros.”

Late day. Climb the Needles Highway through the granite spires and the tight Needle’s Eye tunnel, ending at Sylvan Lake for a walk. Dusk is prime for wildlife on the drive home.

Flex note. This is a genuinely full day. If it runs long, drop the Wildlife Loop — your park pass is good all week, so catch it another evening.

02
TUE · Sep 15

The carved mountains

  • Scenic approachIron Mountain Rd (US-16A) — pigtail bridges + framing tunnels
  • RushmoreNo entry fee · parking $10 (good all year)
  • Evening optionRushmore lighting — confirm current time at the park

Morning. Take Iron Mountain Road in as your scenic approach — it’s built to frame Rushmore through its tunnels. At the memorial, walk the Presidential Trail (0.6-mi loop right underneath) and the Sculptor’s Studio.

Midday. Lunch in Keystone or Hill City.

Afternoon. About 40 minutes to Crazy Horse Memorial: the in-progress carving, the Indian Museum of North America, and a bus ride to the base.

Evening. A lighter-driving day by design — if you skipped Sunday’s lit-up Rushmore, circle back tonight. The program shortens after peak summer, so check the current time.

03
WED · Sep 16

Out to the Badlands

  • Drive out≈ 1 h 30 east via I-90
  • Badlands entry$30/vehicle — good 7 days
  • On the wayWall Drug: 5¢ coffee, homemade donuts, the “backyard”
  • OptionalMinuteman Missile NHS — Cold War silo, right off I-90

The drive. The longest day trip of the week, but worth it. Break the interstate at Wall Drug — pure kitsch you’ll have seen billboards for over 40 miles.

Midday. Enter the Badlands and drive the Loop Road (SD-240): pull-right-up overlooks and short boardwalk trails (Door, Window, Notch). Watch for bighorn sheep and bison.

Optional. Right off the interstate near the exit, the Minuteman Missile site is a genuinely eerie stop — a preserved launch silo and control facility.

Heading back. Sunset in the Badlands is spectacular but means a ~9:30 return; most likely you’ll turn homeward late afternoon.

04
THU · Sep 17

Into the northern hills

  • DirectionNorth on US-385 — your inn’s best-placed day
  • CanyonSpearfish Canyon Byway (US-14A) — Roughlock Falls is a short walk
  • DinnerJacobs Brewhouse (open Thu) or Saloon No. 10 for atmosphere

Morning. Drive the Spearfish Canyon Scenic Byway, a limestone gorge stitched with waterfalls. Roughlock Falls is the standout — short, easy, and lovely, with the first fall color possibly turning.

Afternoon. On to Deadwood: gold-rush Main Street, the Wild Bill Hickok saga (Saloon No. 10 has the history and daily reenactments), and Mount Moriah Cemetery above town, where Wild Bill and Calamity Jane are buried, with a sweeping overlook.

Dinner. Jacobs Brewhouse has the best food in town and is open Thursdays; Saloon No. 10 wins on pure atmosphere.

05
FRI · Sep 18

The long road home

  • MorningBreakfast, then point the car east
  • The haul≈ 9–9.5 hrs to the Twin Cities via I-90
  • Last looksWall Drug & the Badlands sit right on I-90 east

Departure. One last inn breakfast, then aim east on I-90. This is a long driving day — roughly nine hours to the Twin Cities — so weigh any detours against how late you want to arrive.

On the way out. Wall Drug and even the Badlands sit directly on your route, so if Wednesday felt rushed, a short second look is “free” mileage-wise. In Rapid City itself, the downtown City of Presidents bronzes are a five-minute leg-stretch before you commit to the interstate. After that, it’s cornfields and podcasts to Minnesota.

Two easy swaps & add-ons

Devils Tower. If a monolith appeals more than moonscapes, trade the Badlands for Devils Tower — a 1.6-mile paved loop circles the base. It’s a long-ish drive west, so it wants a full day of its own.

Minuteman Missile. Bolt onto the Badlands day — it’s right off the same interstate exit, and it’s on your drive home too.

On passes. The America the Beautiful pass ($80/yr) only pays off across three-plus fee parks, and it does not cover cave-tour tickets. Paying per park (Badlands $30, Devils Tower $25) is likely cheaper.

Book the cave first. Wind Cave’s Garden of Eden tour is the one fixed-time thing all week. Reserve it on recreation.gov before you leave home.
